findings:
🟠 [wdog-stale-pid-fallback] MUST-FIX `_watchdog_signal_worker` falls back to a bare-pid `kill "-$sig" "$target"` when the process-group kill fails. On every path WORKER_SID is a group leader (setsid no-fork: sid==rp; fork: session-leader child; set -m: captured pgid), so the group kill always suffices while the worker is alive; the fallback can only ever hit a stale target. Concrete failure: the dispatcher dies abnormally (harness dead-man kill, trapped signal) leaving the token file in place and the setsid'd sleeper alive in its own session; up to `--timeout` later the subshell fires, the group is gone, and the fallback TERMs then (10 s later) KILLs whatever process now owns that recycled pid — exactly the "kill of a recycled pid" the spec forbids. Smallest remediation: delete the `|| kill "-$sig" "$target"` fallback, pass `$rp` into `_arm_worker_watchdog`, and `kill -0 "$rp" || exit 0` before each signal.
🟡 [wdog-no-cancel-on-signal-exit] CUT/FOLLOW-UP Watchdog cancellation lives only in `_wait_worker_with_watchdog`; no exit/terminal trap calls `_cancel_worker_watchdog`, so a dispatcher exiting via a trapped signal leaves the sleeper, subshell and `/tmp/hetero-wdog-tok-*` files behind (they also inherit WT_LOCK_FD). Follow-up: invoke `_cancel_worker_watchdog` from the existing `_cont_terminal_on_exit` handler. Excluded now: spec requires reaping on normal exit, which the tests prove; abnormal-exit leakage is pre-existing behaviour for the worker too.
🟡 [detached-path-no-reap] CUT/FOLLOW-UP Detached-child path now runs the worker in its own session (setsid) yet still `return 0`s before `reap_container`; descendants that leave the worker's pgrp survive the timeout KILL and are no longer inside the detached child's session for any end-of-run cleanup. Excluded now: the bound itself is enforced and tested on that path (assert_detached_path_enforced_timeout_kills), and base had the same early return; confirm reap_container semantics before extending it there.
🔵 [set-m-plain-path] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The setsid-absent fallback enables `set -m` globally for the rest of the script; with a controlling tty a backgrounded worker reading stdin stops on SIGTTIN, and later `&` jobs (heartbeat etc.) get their own pgrps. Excluded: util-linux setsid is present on all target hosts and no test host reaches this branch.
🔵 [test-pgrep-host-wide] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `assert_r1_no_stray_watchdog` runs `pgrep -f 'hetero-wall-watchdog'` host-wide, so any concurrent enforced dispatch on the same box fails the suite. Excluded: Verify runs are solo/sequential per the brief; tighten to this run's tag later.
